.KEY MESSAGES...
Updated at 1212 AM CDT Sun Sep 20 2026

- Low chances (15-30%) for showers or storms across the Hill Country 
  and Southern Edwards Plateau from Sunday night into Tuesday.

- Low chances (10-30%) for spotty rain across South Central Texas 
  through next week with most staying dry.

- Above average temperatures continue into next weekend.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Monday)
Issued at 1212 AM CDT Sun Sep 20 2026

Another warm day is in the cards for Sunday. Southwesterly flow 
aloft should continue to push cirrus across the area, which will 
blunt insolation some during the afternoon. High temperatures are 
still forecast to reach the 90s across South Central Texas with a 
few isolated spots briefly nudging above 100F. A shortwave trough 
embedded within the southwesterly flow will track across the Edwards 
Plateau late afternoon into the evening. This is expected to trigger 
showers and thunderstorms, beginning primarily northwest of the area 
closer to the dry line. While this area has better kinematic support 
for development, the zone of storm development could be sensitive to 
where the cirrus is thinnest, which may shift storm formation closer 
to the Hill Country as depicted in some of the REFS members. In 
either case, weak steering flow indicates a few storms could slowly 
push into the Hill Country and southern Edwards Plateau in the 
evening hours before instability wears off around midnight and the 
potential fizzles out. Rain chances range from 15 to 30 percent over 
those areas Sunday night. While severe weather is unlikely given the 
lack of noteworthy wind shear, gusty winds are possible with high 
1200+ J/kg DCAPE depicted in the HREF means. Slow storm movement may 
also support locally heavier rains.

The passage of the shortwave trough should weaken the overhead ridge 
some on Monday, though emerging anticyclonic flow at Z250 over 
Mexico and a lack of additional upstream impulses of energy means 
the ridge will have some time to recuperate. Temperatures will stay 
unseasonably hot with highs remaining in the 90s to around 100F and 
lows not varying much from the consistent 70s. Despite the lack of 
vorticity aloft, a weak front is forecast to move into North Texas 
and then slow to a stall beneath the ridge over West Central Texas, 
possibly interacting with any leftover boundaries deposited by 
Sunday night's convective activity. This provides a window for 
spotty showers and thunderstorms Monday afternoon/evening, again for 
the southern Edwards Plateau and Hill Country, and possibly into the 
Austin metro area as well. Given the lack of strong forcing, 
confidence is low and rain chances range from 15 to 30 percent. 

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Monday night through Saturday)
Issued at 1212 AM CDT Sun Sep 20 2026

Zonal flow aloft through the midweek over South Central Texas means 
the weak front is unlikely to advance much farther south into our 
area. Nonetheless, its accompanying band of higher theta-e and 
moisture stuck beneath mid-level ridging, as well as areally lower 
convective inhibition, will support low chances for isolated rain 
(with chances ranging up to 30 percent) through Wednesday. 
Temperatures are expected to stay unseasonably warm, the 
opportunities for slight relief from spotty rains and associated 
puffs of cloudiness allow the distribution of forecast temperatures 
from ensembles to gradually trend slightly cooler towards the end of 
the upcoming week. The overall model blend is not optimistic, 
budging only a few degrees downwards, though the statistical 
guidance is slightly more optimistic and suggests increased coverage 
of highs in the low to mid 90s by the week's end. Lows are likely to 
remain unseasonably mild, but there are hints in the ensemble 
guidance that drier continental air could penetrate into East Texas 
in the latter half of the week and help reduce low-level moisture 
enough to lower overnight temperatures.

Ridging remains over the area into the weekend, keeping rain chances 
low. To the west, a strong plume of moisture is expected to kick 
into gear as deep southerly flow intensifies on the western 
periphery of the ridge. While the bulk of the moisture will be well 
west of the area, a bolstered easterly flow from the Gulf running up 
the Rio Grande in response to the jet streak aloft keeps the low 
possibility of isolated rains over the Rio Grande Plains in the 
forecast through the week. &&

.AVIATION...
(06Z TAFS)
Issued at 1212 AM CDT Sun Sep 20 2026

VFR ceilings are expected, however there is a non-zero chance for
some MVFR ceilings at AUS. Winds remain east-southeasterly around
5-10 kts, but will likely be calm to less than 5 kts through mid-
morning. High clouds from decaying convection out west will result
in BKN clouds at 25k feet through the night.
